provenance.purpose: I3 Step 1 — frozen record of the artifact-distribution baseline before any manifest-contract work. Evidence classes are separated: repository_baseline is read from source at the recorded commit; deployed_observation is what the live staging service and R2 objects returned on the recorded date; inferred entries are conclusions not directly proven; unavailable_evidence lists what could not be verified from this repository.
provenance.generated_by: backend engineering — I3 step 1 baseline freeze
provenance.drift_check: tests/baseline/baseline-drift.test.ts rebuilds the real application, requests GET /config and fails if the response differs in any field, value or canonical hash from repository_baseline.response

repository_baseline.implementation: src/routes/config.ts — a static literal; the only runtime input is ARTIFACT_BASE_URL, which prefixes each artifact url
repository_baseline.authentication: none — public endpoint by design; the mobile app bootstraps from it before any other call
repository_baseline.error_behavior: the route cannot fail by itself (no I/O); the global handler returns { error: { statusCode, message } } for 404/429/5xx; /config does not depend on the database, so a database outage does not affect it
environment_specific_behavior: artifact url prefix comes from ARTIFACT_BASE_URL per environment
CORS: origin allowlist plus GET/POST/OPTIONS only when NODE_ENV=production, permissive otherwise
/version reports NODE_ENV as environment; /config payload itself is identical in every environment
repository_baseline.response_canonicalization: JSON with object keys sorted recursively, no whitespace, UTF-8

storage_convention.immutability_rule: a released object key is never rewritten; any content change requires a new version, filename and hash (enforced by review process and by UNIQUE (artifact, version) in artifact_versions)

repository_baseline.rollback_mechanism: a /config-only change: edit src/routes/config.ts back to the previous version string, url and hash; every prior version remains addressable on R2 (docs/DEPLOYMENT.md section 7). Requires engineering lead approval like a forward release. No automated selection exists.
compatibility_expectations: the mobile app treats /config as its bootstrap and must always consume artifact urls from this response, never construct them
top-level shape is exactly { version, country, artifacts } with exactly the four artifact keys above
each artifact descriptor carries exactly { version, url, hash, release_date, country }
hash format is sha256:<64 hex> over the exact object bytes
the E9.1 beta freeze forbids changing any of the four artifact versions without engineering lead approval

health_endpoint.note: consistent with the known Supabase free-tier idle pause (third occurrence pattern predicted in PROGRESS.md 2026-08-14); /config and /version were unaffected, as designed. Restoration is a manual engineering-lead action and is outside this task's scope.

inferred: mobile consumes artifacts.<name>.version, .url and .hash (documented contract: version for cache comparison, url for download, hash for integrity); release_date and country are informational — inferred from docs/DEPLOYMENT.md and PROGRESS.md, not verified against mobile source, which is not accessible from this repository

no caching layer sits in front of /config (cf-cache-status DYNAMIC, no cache-control anywhere), so clients see changes on next request; effective cache duration is therefore zero at the CDN and client-policy-defined on device
production serves the identical /config payload if deployed, since the payload is environment-independent; the existence and state of a production deployment was not observed
unavailable_evidence: mobile repository source (fields actually read from /config) — recorded above as inferred
R2 bucket name, account configuration and object metadata beyond public HTTP responses
Render service configuration and environment variable values (deliberately not enumerated here)
wellapath-knowledge-base repository content at commit c1b07944ea0b231914943ac17b2265441e53b85c (commit id relayed by task instruction; repository not accessible from here)
known_gaps: no Cache-Control headers on /config or on R2 artifact objects: cache behavior is client-defined, not contract-defined
artifact hashes are declared by /config but the backend never verifies them against R2 at serve time; verification happens at release time (process) and on device (mobile)
no manifest signing; integrity relies on TLS to an approved origin plus the sha256 in /config
GET /internal/metrics is unauthenticated (pre-external-beta item, docs/TELEMETRY_OPERATIONS.md section 7)
rollback is a manual code change with no machine-readable last-known-good record
